guide.title: Morris Park, the Bronx: Racecourse Lots and Hospital Campuses
guide.intro: Morris Park is a neighborhood in the East Bronx, part of Bronx Community District 11, with ZIP codes 10461 and 10462. The 2020 census counted 25,077 residents across 0.347 square miles: 42.5% White (non-Hispanic), 33.2% Hispanic or Latino of any race, 14.1% Asian and 6.7% Black (non-Hispanic). The neighborhood has an Italian-American population and an Albanian-American presence, and Arthur Avenue and Morris Park are viewed as the Bronx's primary Italian American communities. Morris Park Avenue carries the library, the restaurants, John Dormi & Sons Funeral Home and the Albert Einstein College of Medicine's Jack and Pearl Resnick Campus, while the hospitals stand on Pelham Parkway South, Eastchester Road and Waters Place. Neill Avenue and Pelham Parkway bound it to the north, Eastchester Road to the east. The name comes from John Albert Morris, who built the Morris Park Racecourse; after a fire in 1910 the property was divided into lots for the current neighborhood.

sections.heading: Morris Park Avenue and the hospital campuses
sections.body:
Morris Park Avenue carries most of the neighborhood's addresses: the Morris Park Library at 985, the Morris Park Inn at 1024, Patricia's of Morris Park at 1082, John Dormi & Sons Funeral Home at 1121, which Joseph Garofalo, a World War II veteran, persuaded to display his collection of medals and war memorabilia, naming it the Bronx Military Museum, and the Albert Einstein College of Medicine's Jack and Pearl Resnick Campus at 1300. Loreto Park is bounded by Morris Park, Haight, Van Nest and Tomlinson Avenues, and is named for Alfred Loreto, a police officer of 1870 Hering Avenue who was killed on July 21, 1950 while foiling an attempted kidnapping of his neighbor. The park was renovated in 2012 at a cost of about $500,000 and reconstructed in 2021 and 2022 at about $2,000,000, reopening in April 2022.

The hospitals stand off the avenue. Jacobi Medical Center is at 1400 Pelham Parkway South, Calvary Hospital at 1740 Eastchester Road, Montefiore Medical Center's Jack D. Weiler Hospital at 1825 Eastchester Road, and Bronx Psychiatric Center at 1500 Waters Place. The college's site was chosen for ample land and proximity to the adjacent Bronx Municipal Hospital, then under construction — the hospital that opened in 1955 as the Bronx Municipal Hospital Center and is now Jacobi. Jacobi and Einstein were the first medical school and municipal hospital to enter into a formal affiliation agreement at the same time they were both built.

Morris Park is bounded by Neill Avenue and Pelham Parkway to the north, Eastchester Road to the east, the Amtrak Northeast Corridor tracks and Sackett Avenue to the east and south, and Bronxdale Avenue and White Plains Road to the west. It borders Van Nest to its southwest, Parkchester and Westchester Square to its south, and Pelham Parkway to its northeast.

The neighborhood's Columbus Day parade began in 1977, and Tony LoBianco, Chazz Palminteri, Regis Philbin and Joe Pepitone are among its past Grand Marshals. After Italy won the 2006 World Cup, over 30,000 flocked to the neighborhood for an all-day party. Notable people from Morris Park include Cara Buono (b. 1971), Mary Higgins Clark (1927–2020), Jake LaMotta (1922–2017) and Andrew Velazquez (b. 1994).

sections.heading: The racecourse and the lots it left
sections.body:
John Albert Morris was the majority shareholder of the Morris Park Racecourse and Leonard W. Jerome its president. The track opened on August 20, 1889, with the jockey Isaac Murphy riding on opening day, on land in a part of Westchester County that was annexed into the Bronx in 1895. It hosted the Preakness Stakes in 1890, and the Belmont Stakes was run there from 1890. Thoroughbred racing continued until the final race on October 15, 1904.

The property outlasted the racing. Automobile racing followed, and the Aeronautic Society of New York leased the grounds as an aerodrome from 1907 to 1909, with Glenn Curtiss giving a flying exhibition there in June 1909. Fire damaged the stables on April 10, 1910, after which the property was divided into lots for the current neighborhood; by 1921 the former clubhouse had become a factory to manufacture ornamental iron.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body:
The local subway is the IRT Dyre Avenue Line, the 5 train, which runs under the Esplanade. Morris Park station stands at Paulding Avenue and Esplanade, is served by the 5 at all times, and serves both Morris Park and Pelham Parkway. It opened on May 29, 1912 under the New York, Westchester and Boston Railway and closed on December 12, 1937; on May 15, 1941 a shuttle service was implemented between Dyre Avenue and East 180th Street. The station is Spanish Mission style, designed by Alfred T. Fellheimer, who also led design work on Grand Central Terminal, and it was listed on the National Register of Historic Places on July 6, 2005.

No Metro-North station currently serves Morris Park. A Metro-North station named Morris Park is planned on the New Haven Line as part of Penn Station Access, alongside new stations at Co-op City, Parkchester/Van Nest and Hunts Point. In August 2024 the New York City Council voted to rezone 46 city blocks in Parkchester, Van Nest and Morris Park around the Parkchester/Van Nest and Morris Park stations, as part of the same project. Phase One is tentatively targeted for 2027; as of October 2025, three of the four stations could still open as early as 2027 if Amtrak agreed to expedite the work, but the Hunts Point station would still be delayed.

The Bx21 runs between Mott Haven, at East 138th Street and Lincoln Avenue, and Westchester Square, at Westchester Avenue and Lane Avenue, with Third Avenue, Boston Road and Morris Park Avenue among its primary streets. The Bx39 runs between Clasons Point, at Soundview Avenue and Cornell Avenue, and Wakefield, at East 241st Street and White Plains Road, primarily via White Plains Road, the neighborhood's western boundary; it has a third terminus at Williamsbridge, at White Plains Road and Gun Hill Road, served overnight only and also reached via White Plains Road. A T113 shuttle bus is listed as running on Morris Park Avenue and Williamsbridge Road between East 180th Street and Eastchester–Dyre Avenue.

The Amtrak Northeast Corridor tracks form part of the neighborhood's boundary.

faq.question: How do I get to Morris Park?
faq.answer: The local subway is the IRT Dyre Avenue Line, the 5 train, which runs under the Esplanade; Morris Park station stands at Paulding Avenue and Esplanade and is served by the 5 at all times. By bus, the Bx21 runs between Mott Haven and Westchester Square with Morris Park Avenue among its primary streets, and the Bx39 runs primarily via White Plains Road, the neighborhood's western boundary, between Clasons Point and Wakefield. No Metro-North station currently serves Morris Park, though one named Morris Park is planned on the New Haven Line as part of Penn Station Access.

faq.question: Why is it called Morris Park?
faq.answer: The neighborhood is named after John Albert Morris, who built the Morris Park Racecourse. Morris was the racecourse's majority shareholder and Leonard W. Jerome its president. The track opened on August 20, 1889 on land in a part of Westchester County annexed into the Bronx in 1895, and after a fire in 1910 the property was divided into lots for the current neighborhood.

faq.question: What happened to the Morris Park Racecourse?
faq.answer: Thoroughbred racing ran until the final race on October 15, 1904, but the grounds stayed in use. Automobile racing followed, and the Aeronautic Society of New York leased the site as an aerodrome from 1907 to 1909, with Glenn Curtiss giving a flying exhibition there in June 1909. Fire damaged the stables on April 10, 1910, the property was divided into building lots, and by 1921 the former clubhouse had become a factory to manufacture ornamental iron.

faq.question: Which hospitals are in Morris Park?
faq.answer: Jacobi Medical Center, at 1400 Pelham Parkway South, is one of NYC Health + Hospitals' 11 acute care facilities, with 457 beds, a Level I Adult Trauma Center, a Level II Pediatric Trauma Center and the Bronx's only burn unit. Calvary Hospital is at 1740 Eastchester Road and Montefiore Medical Center's 431-bed Jack D. Weiler Hospital at 1825 Eastchester Road. Bronx Psychiatric Center, at 1500 Waters Place, is state-operated, with 156 adult inpatient beds. The Albert Einstein College of Medicine, at 1300 Morris Park Avenue, is a medical school rather than a hospital.

faq.question: Is there a library in Morris Park?
faq.answer: Yes. The Morris Park Library, at 985 Morris Park Avenue, became the neighborhood's first library when it opened on July 21, 2006. The two-level, 6,600-square-foot branch holds a collection of 25,000 adult, young adult and children's books, audio recordings and resources in English, Italian, Albanian and Chinese, along with 19 public-access computers and wireless internet.

photos.title: Morris Park station platform above the neighborhood
photos.description: The open-air platform of the Morris Park subway station on a bright overcast day in June 2018. A black sign lettered Morris Park hangs in a frame on the blue-green railing at the platform edge, and dark steel masts with lit amber lamps run along the concrete deck to the right. Beyond the railing the ground drops away to a residential street lined with parked cars, leafy trees, low brick houses and garages, with an apartment tower on the horizon.
photos.author: Adam Moss from Tonawanda, New York, United States

places.name: Albert Einstein College of Medicine
places.summary: A medical school on the Jack and Pearl Resnick Campus at 1300 Morris Park Avenue. Its own site states that the college operates patient care services across more than 300 patient-care locations in New York City, Westchester and the Hudson Valley. It operates as an independent degree-granting institution within the Montefiore Einstein Health System, an authority it achieved in 2019.
places.history: Planning was initiated in 1945 by Samuel Belkin, president of Yeshiva University. The college was founded in 1953; Albert Einstein agreed to lend his name on March 14, 1953, and the first class of 56 students arrived on September 12, 1955. It was the first new medical school to open in New York City since 1897 and the first in the United States to open under Jewish auspices. The site was chosen for ample land and proximity to the adjacent Bronx Municipal Hospital, then under construction. By 2008 expansion, including a $225 million research complex, had doubled the size of Einstein's campus to nearly 40 acres.

photos.title: Albert Einstein College of Medicine at dusk
photos.description: An elevated view over the campus at dusk, with an orange and violet sky above the low-rise Bronx skyline. The brick tower at left carries the Einstein wordmark reading Albert Einstein College of Medicine; lit windows and a glass-fronted entrance are visible on the grey building at centre, with a curved pale-stone building and a long white block to the right.
photos.author: HAL333

places.name: Jacobi Medical Center
places.summary: A hospital at 1400 Pelham Parkway South with 457 beds, one of NYC Health + Hospitals' 11 acute care facilities, serving approximately 1.2 million residents. It is a Level I Adult Trauma Center and a Level II Pediatric Trauma Center, and it houses the Bronx's only burn unit.
places.history: Established in 1955 as the Bronx Municipal Hospital Center, it opened for pediatric and infant care on November 1, 1955 with 898 beds. Its affiliation with the Albert Einstein College of Medicine was the first time a medical school and municipal hospital entered into a formal affiliation agreement at the same time they were both built. The hospital is named for the German physician Abraham Jacobi, regarded as the father of American pediatrics.

photos.title: Jacobi Medical Center from the air
photos.description: An aerial view of the hospital campus, photographed in March 2007. A rooftop sign on the pale tower at centre reads Jacobi Medical Center. A red brick wing with a glazed stair tower stands to the right, an ambulance is parked under the entrance canopy below it, and surface car parks, bare winter trees and low-rise Bronx housing surround the site.
photos.author: Zoirusha at English Wikipedia

places.name: Calvary Hospital
places.summary: A hospital at 1740 Eastchester Road, described as one of the first, and still one of the largest, medical complexes focusing on end-of-life hospice care. Its own site describes it as the country's only fully accredited acute care specialty hospital exclusively providing palliative care for adult patients with advanced cancer and other life-limiting illnesses.
places.history: Established in 1899 and affiliated with the Archdiocese of New York. It operates 225 beds across multiple locations, including a 25-bed unit at Lutheran Medical Center in Sunset Park, Brooklyn, held since 2001, and the 10-bed Dawn Greene Hospice on the 15th floor of the Mary Manning Walsh Home on Manhattan's Upper East Side.

places.name: Jack D. Weiler Hospital
places.summary: Montefiore Medical Center's 431-bed hospital, also known as Einstein Hospital, adjacent to the Albert Einstein College of Medicine. The operator's own site gives it as the Jack D. Weiler Hospital—Einstein Campus, at 1825 Eastchester Road, with the telephone number 718-904-2000.

places.name: Bronx Psychiatric Center
places.summary: A state-operated psychiatric hospital at 1500 Waters Place, managed by the New York State Office of Mental Health. It provides 156 adult inpatient beds, along with an 86-bed children's psychiatric center and a 188-bed residential village, on an 85-acre campus.
places.history: It opened in 1963 as a state mental health facility in the northeast Bronx. It is part of the Bronx Behavioral Health Campus, a 436,000-square-foot complex that opened in 2015 and 2016.

places.name: Loreto Park
places.summary: A park bounded by Morris Park, Haight, Van Nest and Tomlinson Avenues, named after Alfred Loreto, a police officer of 1870 Hering Avenue who was killed on July 21, 1950 while foiling an attempted kidnapping of his neighbor.
places.history: The park was renovated in 2012 at a cost of about $500,000. A reconstruction in 2021 and 2022, costing about $2,000,000, was followed by a reopening in April 2022.

places.name: Morris Park Library
places.summary: A New York Public Library branch at 985 Morris Park Avenue. The two-level, 6,600-square-foot branch houses a collection of 25,000 adult, young adult and children's books, audio recordings and resources in English, Italian, Albanian and Chinese, and has 19 public-access computers and wireless internet.
places.history: The Morris Park branch became the neighborhood's first library when it opened on July 21, 2006.

photos.title: Entrance to the Morris Park Library
photos.description: The library entrance seen from the pavement in March 2022, with sidewalk scaffolding erected across the frontage. An awning above the doors reads Morris Park Branch, the street number 985 is lettered on the door glass, and notices fill the window bays to the left. A wheeled book cart signed Morris Park Community Cart stands beside the doorway, where a man in a black shirt is browsing.
photos.author: Jim.henderson

places.name: Bronx Military Museum
places.summary: Joseph Garofalo, a World War II veteran, persuaded John Dormi & Sons Funeral Home, at 1121 Morris Park Avenue, to display his collection of medals and war memorabilia, and named it the Bronx Military Museum. The funeral home's own site gives its address in that form and its telephone number as (718) 863-2000.

places.name: Patricia's of Morris Park
places.summary: A restaurant at 1082 Morris Park Avenue. Its own site describes it as a blend of the casual and sophisticated, mixing the more sophisticated and nuanced service and cuisine of a fine Ristorante with a casual charm of a classic Italian Bar/Restaurant, and gives its telephone number as (718) 409-9069.

places.name: Morris Park Inn
places.summary: A restaurant at 1024 Morris Park Avenue. Its own site self-categorizes it as an American Restaurant, gives its telephone number as 718-239-4109, and states that it offers online ordering through Uber Eats and GrubHub, catering and event hosting.
